archetype.name: Rookie Developmental (checkdown-first)
archetype.definition: An undrafted first-year passer pushed into emergency duty, playing an ultra-conservative, under-the-sticks game while he learns to process at NFL speed.

report.headline: Emergency rookie whose checkdown-only approach hasn't avoided turnovers or moved the chains
report.take:
Joe Fagnano is the Ravens' third quarterback by circumstance, not by design. Lamar Jackson's thumb surgery and Tyler Huntley's season-ending toe injury pushed an undrafted rookie from Connecticut and Maine into the lineup. His two appearances came in brutal conditions. Week 8 was relief duty in a 36-10 loss at Buffalo, where he was pressured on 52% of his dropbacks and blitzed 13 times. Week 9 was his first start, on four days' rest, against a Jacksonville defense that now ranks third. That context matters, because the raw line is about as bad as a qualified quarterback can post: 3.87 yards per attempt and 0.77 adjusted net yards per dropback, both last of 49, with -0.601 EPA per dropback.

The defining trait is how short everything is. His intended air yards sit at 3.89, and he throws an average of 5.32 yards short of the sticks. Thirty-three of his 39 charted attempts were under 10 air yards, and those plays cost -20.4 EPA. The throws behind the line were the worst of it: 11 attempts at -1.027 EPA apiece with an 18% success rate. This isn't a gunslinger making bad decisions downfield. It's a passer who isn't getting the ball out to anywhere useful, and whose checkdowns haven't been accurate either: CPOE on short throws is -13.9.

What the totals hide is that the two games failed in different ways. In Buffalo it was a collapsing pocket and wild accuracy, with a 23.8% bad-throw rate and -16.4 CPOE. Against Jacksonville the pocket was cleaner (25% pressured) and his ball placement tightened up (6.7% bad throws, -5.8 CPOE). But he got even more timid, with intended air yards of 2.4, and two interceptions produced -15.5 EPA in a game where he barely threw past the line. The other striking split is Zay Flowers. Nine targets to the team's top receiver cost -18.3 EPA, and all three interceptions went to the left side. Six targets to Mark Andrews, meanwhile, were positive at +0.335 per target. There is no rhythm with the No. 1 receiver yet.

Going forward, he is a placeholder until Jackson's estimated mid-December return. That return date is an estimate, and the depth chart listing him as QB2 means even his starting status isn't locked in. The ceiling is a mistake-free game manager behind a run-leaning offense. The interception rate (7.7%) is too extreme to persist on this volume, but nothing yet suggests he can create yards on his own.

strengths.title: Cleaner mechanics once given a pocket
strengths.body: When Jacksonville let him set his feet, his bad-throw rate fell to 6.7% and his CPOE improved by more than ten points over the Buffalo relief outing. That points to the Week 8 accuracy collapse being a product of the pressure, not a fixed flaw. It is a single game, but it is the most encouraging thing on the tape.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks under heavy pressure
strengths.body: He's been pressured on 41.9% of dropbacks, among the worst rates in the league. Yet his pressure-to-sack rate of 22.2% ranks 10th of 42, and his two scrambles were positive plays. For an undrafted rookie behind a line that ranks 26th in hits allowed, keeping pressure from turning into drive-killing sacks is a real survival skill.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws and Andrews work
strengths.body: On the rare occasions he's pushed the ball 10+ yards, he's been roughly break-even: -0.008 EPA per play and a CPOE of 0.2. Andrews is the only top target he's produced positive value with. Six attempts is a hint, not a fact, but it says the coaching staff could unlock more by asking him to throw over the middle rather than behind the line.

concerns.title: Everything lives short of the sticks
concerns.body: He throws an average of 5.32 yards short of the line to gain, and his under-10 attempts have bled -20.4 EPA. That is the cost of the conservative approach without its payoff: a conservative passer has to be accurate, and his short-throw CPOE is -13.9. This is the core issue, and it grew more extreme in his start. Expect it to persist as long as he's learning on the fly.

concerns.title: Turnovers on low-risk throws
concerns.body: An interception rate of 7.7% ranks 48th of 49, and he has two turnover-worthy fumbles to go with three picks in under 50 dropbacks. Turning the ball over while throwing this short is the worst combination. The rate will come down on more volume, since three picks in 39 throws is partly variance, but he hasn't shown the processing to keep it near the league's 2.4%.

concerns.title: No connection with Zay Flowers
concerns.body: Flowers drew nine targets that cost -18.3 EPA, the single biggest hole in his season. All three interceptions came on throws to the left. Rookie backups often lack reps with the starting group, so better practice time could fix part of this. Until it does, the offense's best receiver is a liability with him under center.

trend.note: Both games were deeply negative, but for different reasons. Week 8 was chaotic accuracy under a heavy rush. Week 9 brought cleaner ball placement but even shorter throws and two interceptions, so there's no real upward slope yet.

nextGame.headline: Softer defense, friendly script, but he must stop the giveaways
nextGame.body:
The Chargers are a much gentler test than Jacksonville. Their pass defense ranks 17th by EPA, their sack rate is 23rd, and their offense is the league's worst by EPA while running far more than expected. The Book makes Baltimore a 5.5-point home favorite with a 38.5 total. That points to a low-possession, field-position game where the Ravens can lean on the run and ask Fagnano mostly not to lose it. That suits him, since his worst splits come when trailing big. The catch is that the Chargers' clear weakness is the deep ball (29th in deep EPA), and he hasn't attempted a single throw of 20+ air yards. He also gets 11 days to prepare after a four-day turnaround, his first real week as the starter.

On his side, Jackson is on IR with a mid-December estimated return and Huntley is done for the year. Yet the depth chart lists Fagnano as QB2 as of Nov. 10, so confirm he's actually starting before trusting any of this. For Los Angeles, Justin Herbert is questionable with a finger injury that avoided a fracture. If he plays, the Chargers' offense is less likely to hand Baltimore short fields. Ladd McConkey (back) and DT Justin Eboigbe (ankle) are also questionable. The secondary is thin, with corner Deane Leonard and safety Kendall Williamson out and corner Isas Waxter questionable, though most of those are depth pieces rather than starters.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers' broken offense shapes the script
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles ranks last in offensive EPA and success rate and passes 11.4 points less than expected. If it plays to form, Fagnano works with a lead, on short fields, in a run-first game plan. That shrinks his volume but also his chances to throw it to the other team.

keyMatchups.title: Deep weakness he hasn't tested
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers bleed 1.058 EPA on deep throws, 29th in the league, while being solid underneath. Fagnano's 3.89 intended air yards means he's playing straight into their strength. A couple of designed shots would tell us whether the staff trusts him with more.

keyMatchups.title: Pressure relief from a soft rush
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers' sack rate ranks 23rd, a far cry from the Buffalo game that buried him. With Eboigbe questionable, this could be the cleanest pocket he's seen, which is when his accuracy looked playable.

nextGame.watch: Whether he completes anything to Zay Flowers past the sticks without a turnover. That's the clearest sign of whether the extra preparation week changed anything.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a placeholder run of a few starts until Jackson returns, with the offense built around the run game and short completions. The interception rate is the most likely number to regress, since three picks on 39 attempts is partly bad luck. A league-average rate is a stretch, though, and the pace17 figures of 26 interceptions and 0 touchdowns aren't real in either direction. Passing volume stays low regardless, because Baltimore already passes less than expected and will lean on its defense and run game with him in the lineup. Realistically, he lands around 120 to 185 passing yards a game, with no more than one touchdown and a turnover most weeks.

What would make this sustainable is the Week 9 accuracy holding while he adds a few intermediate throws. The six 10+ air-yard attempts were break-even, which suggests the staff is leaving that on the table. If he stays stuck behind the line, expect more of the same until Jackson's estimated mid-December return. That date is an estimate, and the earlier it comes, the shorter this window gets.
swingFactors: Timing of Lamar Jackson's return from thumb surgery
Whether the staff lets him throw past the sticks
Building any rapport with Zay Flowers

confidence.note: 45 dropbacks across one start and one relief outing, no career history, and an unsettled depth-chart status.
